Published online:
September 3, 2026 (dated: global markets view europe 2026 09 03)

Geographic focus:
Global, with primary focus on US, Europe, Japan

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps recent yield moves, ADP miss, JGB auction, Broadcom earnings
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — NFP Friday, CPI Sept 11, Fed rate decision this month, Waller speech Thursday
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
Bond markets are stabilizing after a bruising stretch, but the macro backdrop remains unfavorable for fixed income. Oil above $90 (US-Iran escalation) is sustaining inflation pressure. Fed rate hike probability for the current month has surged to 67% from 37% a week prior. NY Fed's Williams nudged back slightly, wanting more data. Key near-term catalysts: Waller speech Thursday, NFP Friday, CPI Sept 11. Japan's services sector strength is building BOJ rate hike expectations; the yen rallied on suspected rate check. JGB 30-year auction provided temporary relief after 10Y yields hit a 30-year high. Broadcom flagged strong AI chip demand but sold off in after-hours. Equity futures are modestly positive.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — Fed hike probability, US yields, NFP, CPI, Fed speakers, S&P futures all directly addressed.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (clearly hawkish-leaning; 67% market-implied probability of a hike this month, up sharply from 37%)
Increasing rates magnitude: +25bps (one additional 25bp hike priced as the base case for the upcoming meeting)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (Williams' comment about wanting more data introduces a mild hold-narrative, but it is the minority signal in the article)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Decreasing rates magnitude: 0% — no cut narrative present whatsoever

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: Is it striking a different sentiment/tone compared to previous discussions on US interest rates?
Difference: +55 (More hawkish than before — the sharp jump in hike probability from 37% to 67% in one week signals a meaningful repricing toward tighter policy, with oil and inflation fears as the driver; Williams' softening is a footnote, not the dominant signal)

Q06. Focus on the very latest information: How does it compare to previous information on US interest rates?
Difference: +55 (The repricing from 37% to 67% hike odds in a single week is a significant hawkish shift in market consensus; persistent oil above $90, strong Japan services data adding global tightening momentum, and Waller's July hawkish lean all reinforce the view that the prior baseline was too dovish)
